title: Teach coding agents reusable skills from passing tests
summary: A developer built MuscleMemory to save reusable skills from coding-agent sessions once tests pass; they report Codex used 30.4% fewer tool calls and 25.5% less input.
agent_role: The coding agent does the task; MuscleMemory captures successful sessions as skills and injects notes later. A human must approve each skill before agents see it.
outcome: Author reports a benchmark with real Codex sessions cut input tokens 25.5%, tool calls 30.4% and time 28.2% with all tasks passing; an early Claude Code run cut input tokens 43.5%.
what_they_did: The author built add-ons for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that record what the agent does. When the automatic tests pass after the last change, it saves a skill. A skill lists the files to change, the test that proves it works, and pitfalls. Skills must pass two later checks and get a person's approval before reuse, and all three agents share them.
how_it_went: The author reports Codex used 25.5% less input text, 30.4% fewer tool calls and 28.2% less time, with all tasks passing. An early Claude Code run cut input by 43.5%. On a small set of real bug-fix tasks, Codex solved as many with about half the text.
worth_knowing: The tests covered repeated tasks on three controlled projects, and the Claude Code run was small. Reusing skills across different projects has not been tested.
prompt: Set up MuscleMemory for this project following its install docs, connect it to [your agent], then work on [task] as usual. After the tests pass, show me the skill it proposes to learn and wait for my approval in the dashboard before keeping it.

curation.rationale: A tool, but the README reports concrete benchmark runs with Codex and Claude Code sessions and a reproduce script. It is still early and the runs are small.
